steps.label: Dos frases
steps.sentence: I have a colleague. She speaks four languages.

steps.label: Pronombre sujeto
steps.sentence: I have a colleague **who** speaks four languages.
steps.change: “She” se reemplaza por “who”; no se puede quitar porque es el sujeto.

steps.label: Dos frases
steps.sentence: This is the film. We saw it last night.

steps.label: Pronombre objeto
steps.sentence: This is the film **(that)** we saw last night.
steps.change: “it” desaparece; “that” es objeto, así que puedes omitirlo.

B1-1-0.title: ¿Who, which, that… o nada?
B1-1-0.question: ¿A qué se refiere el pronombre y qué función cumple en su cláusula?

branches.if: Es una persona y es el sujeto
branches.example: The woman who called left a message.

branches.if: Es una cosa y es el sujeto
branches.example: It’s an app that works offline.

branches.if: Es objeto (persona o cosa): después viene otro sujeto
branches.example: The book (that) I lent you is mine.
That’s the colleague whose laptop was stolen.

items.b: The song that I like it.
items.note: La segunda está mal: “that” ya es el objeto, no repitas “it”.

items.a: The people who work here are kind.
items.b: The people work here are kind.
items.note: Sin “who” la frase no tiene sentido: el pronombre sujeto no se puede omitir.

B1-1-1.title: De la situación a la reacción

steps.label: Situación
steps.sentence: People cancel at the last minute.

steps.label: It + verbo + objeto
steps.sentence: **It annoys me when** people cancel at the last minute.
steps.change: “It” es un sujeto vacío; la reacción va primero.

steps.label: It + be + adjetivo
steps.sentence: **It’s frustrating when** people cancel at the last minute.

steps.label: Invertida
steps.sentence: **When** people cancel at the last minute, **it** really annoys me.

items.example: It bothers me when people are late.
It annoys me when the wifi drops.
It upsets me when people lie.
It drives me crazy when he chews loudly.

items.a: It bothers me when he arrives late.
items.b: It bothers me when he will arrive late.
items.note: La segunda está mal: después de “when” va presente simple, no “will”.

items.a: It’s annoying when the bus is late.
items.b: It’s annoying me when the bus is late.
items.note: “It’s annoying” es general; “it’s annoying me” solo describe algo que pasa ahora mismo.
Con “when” hablas de algo que se repite; con “that” comentas un hecho concreto.

steps.label: Gerundio como sujeto
steps.change: El verbo en -ing funciona como sustantivo y lleva verbo en singular.

steps.label: Tras preposición
steps.change: Después de una preposición siempre va -ing.

B1-2-0.title: ¿-ing o to + verbo?
B1-2-0.question: ¿Dónde aparece el verbo en la frase?

branches.if: Es el sujeto de la frase
branches.example: Cooking for ten people is exhausting.

branches.if: Va después de una preposición (in, at, of, before…)
Va después de enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest…
Va después de want, hope, plan, decide…

items.note: El sujeto con gerundio siempre es singular: “is”, aunque diga “reports”.
Después de preposición va -ing, nunca la forma base.

items.a: Not knowing the answer was hard.
items.b: Knowing not the answer was hard.
items.note: La negación va antes del gerundio.

branches.example: This route is shorter and more scenic than that one.
This city has fewer parks than mine.
She works harder than I do.

B1-2-1.title: Qué tan grande es la diferencia

items.example: It’s slightly cheaper than the other one.
This flat is a bit bigger.
The new model is much faster.
Bogotá is a lot colder than Cartagena.
This hotel is far more expensive.
My car is nowhere near as fast as yours.

items.note: Con verbos, “more” va después del verbo.

items.a: The office is better organised now.
items.b: The office is more organiseder now.
items.note: Con participios usa more / better / worse delante, sin -er.
